text:
Recent work supports testing diagnostics against known behavioral relations. “An empirical study on metamorphic testing for recommender systems” (2024) develops six relations and evaluates LibRec, PREA and Surprise, demonstrating reliability testing without exact recommendation labels. This supports checking relationships between paired executions, although it does not establish a validated fault-signature suite for SASRec. [Paper](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0950584924000156). Position-specific studies—[Learning Positional Attention (2024)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2407.02793) and [CAPE (2025)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.09027)—identify positional representations as consequential components, motivating separate attention-path and position-embedding probes.

Practical proposal, inferred from these results: evaluate intact and deliberately modified copies on identical histories and candidates with dropout disabled. Block cross-position attention in every layer; changing earlier items while preserving the final item, length and padding should then leave final-position scores unchanged, provided no other history-mixing path exists. Replace scoring with training-frequency-only scores; fixed-candidate scores should become history-independent and follow frequency ordering, with ties handled explicitly. Shuffle positional embedding rows to test positional disruption, but treat the magnitude and direction of changes as empirical: neither score changes nor accuracy loss are guaranteed, and causal masking can retain order information without positional embeddings.

Calibrate probes by reporting intact-model false alarms, injected-fault detection rates, repeated-seed variability and a fault-by-probe signature matrix. Include candidate-permutation equivariance and future-token isolation as architecture-specific checks. These establish sensitivity to controlled implementation changes; they do not identify causal user preferences, unobserved conformity traits or validation accuracy. Keep macro validation HR@10 as the separate model-selection criterion.
